thread:
matt: thinking about a compact edge->client signal schema for fallbacks and progress so clients can make smarter retry decisions without pulling full traces

julia: +1, we've had bugs where mobile clients retry too aggressively during partial streaming failures

matt: idea: a single header `X-Edge-Signal` with comma-separated key=val pairs. keys: state, progress_pct, resume_token, fallback_hint, ttl_s

kevin: can you sketch the shape? small example pls

matt: sure — example: `X-Edge-Signal: state=partial_fail,progress=42,resume=rtkn_abc123,fallback=small-model,ttl=30`

julia: i like it. ergonomics: clients parse once, then decide: if state=partial_fail && resume present -> try resume path; else if fallback hint -> call fallback model

vivian: what about security/policy? resume tokens are sensitive; should be signed and scoped to conn/session, short TTL

matt: agreed. tokens are opaque to clients; runtime validates on resume. TTL default 30s, minted by edge with tenant id and route id in claim. we send only token id in header, not raw creds

kevin: tradeoffs: adding this header across all responses increases header noise and size, esp for streaming chunks. we should only emit when state != ok or progress changed by >=5%
julia: or emit an initial `state=ok,progress=0` then deltas. but we need to avoid putting too many headers in every chunk — maybe attach as trailer when using chunked encoding and the occasional inline update for important transitions

matt: implementation plan: 1) proto in gateway: signal generator that watches stream slice events; 2) compact serializer -> append to trailer by default; 3) expose option `edge.signal.inline=true` on routes that need live updates for low-latency UX

vivian: fallback interop: we need a canonical string for fallback_hint that maps to model variants (e.g., `fallback=redwood-small-v1`). routing table uses that to decide whether it's compatible

kevin: also need idempotency considerations: if client retries using resume token, runtime should dedupe or apply de-dup window. else the model might double-run side effects
matt: yes — resume token semantics: once-used or one-time-use? proposal: token allows safe replay for N seconds but runtime should attempt at-most-once semantics for side-effecting calls. we can attach `idempotency=soft` as part of the token metadata

julia: can we add a tiny diagnostic field for ops `dbg=slot=12345` so we can correlate with a trace without leaking PII? short opaque id

matt: good call. final example header: `X-Edge-Signal: state=partial_fail,progress=42,resume=rtkn_abc123,fallback=redwood-small-v1,ttl=30,dbg=slot123`

vivian: what's the rollout plan? start with `edge.signal.inline=false` everywhere, enable `inline=true` on mobile routes in a canary and watch for header amplification via console metrics

kevin: also add a circuit-breaker: if more than 0.5% of chunks in a minute emit signals, flip to trailer-only to avoid client bandwidth blowup
matt: i'll draft an RFC with the header grammar, token lifecycle, and runtime knobs. will include sample client pseudocode and a small gRPC/HTTP example (chunked trailer use)

julia: thanks. one more thing: we should version the header: `X-Edge-Signal-v1` to allow future changes without negotiation pain

matt: noted — v1 it is. i'll ping this thread when RFC is up :thumbsup:

infra-bot: deploy-check: gateway schema feature flag `edge_signal_v1` exists in prod flags service (off by default)

vivian: perfect. followups: matt -> RFC; kevin -> dedupe/window behavior; devx -> client pseudocode; ops -> dashboard alerts for header amplification

matt: assigning and will follow up in RFC. thanks everyone
